title: Pick the right motor
about: DC, servo, stepper or brushless: match each job to the best motor.

html: Every motor is good at a different job.
DC gearmotorDC motor + gearboxspinning nonstop, simple speed controlrobot car wheels, toys
Servomotor + sensor + chipmoving to an exact angle and holding itrobot arm joints, steering, grippers
Steppercoils switched in orderexact steps without a sensor3D printers, CNC machines
Brushlessneeds a speed controllervery fast, powerful and efficientdrones, e-bikes, many electric cars
Brushless motors have no brushes rubbing inside. A small computer called an ESC (electronic speed controller) switches the coils instead, so they last longer and waste less energy.
Real robots use a team of motors
• Robot vacuum: DC gearmotors drive its wheels, and another motor spins its brushes.
• Our robot arm: servos at the joints, so each one moves to an exact angle.
• 3D printer: steppers move the nozzle, and small fans cool the plastic.

steps.q: A drone needs motors that spin its propellers super fast without wasting battery. Which kind?
steps.explain: Brushless motors are fast, powerful and efficient. That's why almost every drone uses them.

steps.q: In Bot Arena, what kind of motor would move each joint of a robot's Legs?
steps.explain: Walking robots move each leg joint to an exact angle, which is a servo's job.

steps.q: Which motor would you pick to drive a robot car's wheels?
options: A brushless motor with no speed controller
steps.explain: A DC gearmotor spins nonstop with plenty of torque, which is just what wheels need.
